articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Video game cameras are often a point of contention primarily because a bad one can completely disorient you, or even outright make you feel sick. These are worthwhile things to consider, but I do wish there was more of a discussion around the specific choices that are made in particular camera angles and positions, and how it might actually be important that certain games should be played in the way they are designed. I'm going to throw all of that out of the window right now though and tell you about a Baldur's Gate 3 true third-person camera mod.

articles.description:
If we ignore the many, many negatives that came with the late 90s/early 2000s era of video marketing, there was a certain charm to the edginess that I kind of wish was still around in some ways. I say that because of a recently revealed immersive action horror shooter named Ringwyrm, that, were it to have released in that era, so easily could have had a tagline like, "The only time you'll be happy you've got Ringwyrm." Alas!

articles.description:
Poor Thick as Thieves. When it was revealed over two years ago it had some promise, or at the very least an interesting mechanical premise in that it was a multiplayer immersive sim where everyone would be competing for the same loot. This got downgraded earlier this year ahead of its launch to just solo or co-op play, a real shame but hey ho, how many co-op imsims are there anyway? Sadly, the game has clearly not done well, as a number of layoffs have taken place at developer OtherSide Entertainment following its launch. But at the very least, what's left of the studio has some positive news: it won't become unplayable.
 
Read more

I don't see Sony going back on their plans to embrace a discless PlayStation future, but I do wonder if they realised just how many of us would continue to talk about it for as long as we have. Even RPS got involved, and us PC lot had to abandon discs a millenia ago! And now Sega, former physical media producers themselves, have wandered into the conversation, even throwing a bone to the computer preferring collective that we all are.

The latest FF14 fan festival is taking place, and with that has come a suite of announcements, including a reveal at one of the two new jobs coming as part of the next expansion, Evercold.

I spent most of last Saturday laid out in a Baku hotel room, muscles in both legs ground to flecks of useless meat by the decision to walk down a mountain when there was a perfectly good funicular right there. May this weekend be more fruitful, and less marred by the stupidity of trying to please a step counter that only truly cares about where its next battery charge is coming from. Ruinous silicone bastard.

To recap, it casts you as a medieval vampire fledgling whose family has been abducted by another, boss vampire. You've got 30 days and nights to save your loved ones while deciding just how much you're going to succumb to the gore-guzzling curse.

articles.description:
If the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike’s analogue clickers were all about fine-tuning the sensation at the very tips of your mousing fingers, the HyperX Pulsefire Saga is all about adjusting the parts nestled in the rest of your hand. To nowhere near the same extent, granted, but the Saga’s modular components – and the fact that it costs a fraction of what the X2 Superstrike does – make it appealing addition to your wired mouse options.
Read more
articles.title: HyperX Pulsefire Saga gaming mouse review: modular parts win hearts

I poke my head into the Steam forums as though cracking the door on a suspiciously silent mall.
 Read more

Ah! You hadn't totally retreated from the battlefield following your cancellation in early 2025, Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition's Baltic Powers DLC! articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
It is said that to name a wild thing is to tame it, to delimit and temper it, to defuse its menace. The giant, vaporous spider in Fallgrade is called Karl. Know any Karls? Are you a Karl? I wonder if it's Karl as in Karl Marx. Perhaps it's a reference to arachnid imagery in anti-Communist propaganda, though arachnid imagery isn't the exclusive preserve of anti-Communists.
Myself, I tend to associate the name "Karl" with paperweights, for reasons my brain refuses to explain to me. And yet, for all these steadying associations, Karl the spider still gives me the willies. Nothing tame about that thing at all.
 
Read more
articles.title: I enjoy Fallgrade's grainy physics-defying city almost as much as I fear its foggy giant spider

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
In hindsight, I was a fool for meeting Denshattack’s satirical, irreverent, downright countercultural sensibilities with surprise. Upbeat, even goofy as it is for a train driving game, it shares more common ground with skateboarding games, and while the commodification of skater culture is certainly A Thing, few skaters have ever reapplied their asphalt-eating skills to bootlicking.
What remains striking, though, is how specifically '2026' Denshattack's targets are. The main baddies are a rogue big tech company, deploying all your current favourite social ills: enforced inequality, mass surveillance, misinformation-spewing talking heads, police violence, and soulless AI replacing true craft and skill. If only it did a bit on mass layoffs, it would have had a full set. You meet them with force, too, assembling a crew that resembles a Greatest Hits of Japanese normbreaker groups while repeatedly ramming your engine through those oppressive mechanisms at top-gear Skinkansen speeds.
The result is that Denshattack manages to have it both ways, being fully capable of stretching a daft grin across your face, yet possessing a radical heart that wards off the sense – and, indeed, accusations – that this is just an ironic bit of comedy train capering. Yet according to David Jaumandreu, game director at developers Undercoders, Denshattack was never consciously given a political voice – it simply emerged, logically and naturally, from its Japan being shaped as a more locomotive-mad version of the real one.
Read more
articles.title: "Let's make a better world": Denshattack's developers on counterculture, biker gangs, and the optimism of fighting a mecha with a train

Kingdom Come Deliverance developers Warhorse confirmed back in May that they've got a "new Kingdom Come adventure" in the works, alongside a Lord of the Rings RPG. The name of the former looks like it may now have been revealed via a freshly filed EU trademark for the phrase 'Kingdom Come Salvation'.
Read more

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Perhaps predictably, Creative Assembly's Total War: Warhammer 40,000 could be quite the step change for how Total War handles ranged combat. Yesterday, the developers livestreamed a battle between the Imperium and the Orks, while chatting enthusiastically about the nuances of drop pods and flamers and evasion stats.


Like a gretchin war reporter – there are Ork journalists, right? Newswaaaagh? Gubbinzfeed? The Wall Street Choppa? – I've been running from foxhole to foxhole, jotting down notes. The conclusion I've come to is that the new strategy game could diverge quite significantly from the archers-behind-spearguys square dance of older Twars. Your units are more autonomous and also, more flexible and smarter in terms of who they shoot with what.
 
Read more
articles.title: Sweeping, strafing and suppression: Total War: Warhammer 40,000 threatens to blow up Total War's combat fundamentals

It's set to run until July 27th, so offers a chance to end your week with some superhero graps prior to the game's full launch early next month. Meanwhile, Arc System Works have revealed the first fighter set to arrive as part of Fighting Souls year one batch of post-launch DLC in autumn. It's Phoenix Cyclops.
Read more

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Four years ago, a developer called Jean Nguyen shared a short video on Dwitter of a spinosaurus pulling off a sick combo with Cloud Strife's Buster Sword. This, of course, blew up, but it wasn't actually a game, just some animation work from the dev. And then, somewhere along the line, Nguyen decided to make it into an actual game. It's now called Dinoblade, it's out today, and it is jank and over top in exactly the right ways, and genuinely a rip roaring time.
 
Read more
articles.title: Dinoblade, out now, is equal parts janky, genuinely sick and silly as hell

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Sanctuary: Shattered Sun is the kind of unwholesomely large real-time strategy game where you keep accidentally auto-constructing 50 missile trucks because you were preoccupied with (e.g.) a massive spiderbot offensive on the other side of an ocean. Those things breed like rabbits! Still, easy come, easy go: simply charge your 50 superfluous missile trucks into the nearest line of energy domes, and watch as they, the enemy, and everybody we have ever loved disintegrates in about 20 seconds.
Shattered Sun does reward micromanagement – "every projectile is simulated", the devs proclaim, which means you can dance your tanks away from incoming shells – and also encourages resource efficiency, with a "flow-based economy" that hinges on access to generators and alloy extraction sites. But going by my hour with the demo, it more immediately rewards the act of scooping together a continent-sized deathball and rolling it through the nearest pocket of red on your map.
 Read more
articles.title: I've yet to smash open a Dyson Sphere in sci-fi RTS Sanctuary: Shattered Sun, but I'm enjoying its take on Supreme Commander

The union, who're part of the wider Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB), have called this first meeting "a step in the right direction" and that they've secured "a roadmap for a speedy negotiation process".
Read more

articles.description:
Star Wars Zero Company is the XCOM-style tactics RPG in which you, a Clone Wars-era roughneck called Hawks, lead a squad of "unconventional professionals" into battle against some enigmatic threat to the galaxy. Among these unconventional professionals is a Jedi Padawan, Tel-Rea. Her moves include dual-wielding lightsabers and Force Pushing mooks into overwatch zones. What a beast! Be careful with your Tel-Rea, though: you only get one of her, and she's permakillable. There's no option to train up a replacement Jedi Padawan as a custom operator.
 Read more
articles.title: You only get one, permakillable Jedi Padawan in Star Wars Zero Company, but that's fine because I'm going to roll an R2-D2 deathsquad anyway

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
The machine before me looks like Frankenstein's homebrew version of Guess Who. Its main panel is composed of three rows of portraits. Some show men in 1930s suits, others women in flapper dresses, still more are simply blue people-shaped silhouettes. Below each portrait is a simple on/off switch. To the left of the portraits is a slide selector alongside a list of locations. Above that is a radio dial and filament lights indicating a current setting. At the bottom of the machine is a readout displaying a cryptic code '01-QU-1-11'. And, to the right, most enticing of all, is a big red lever.
It may not be much to look at, but calibrated correctly, this machine lets me hear the dead. It's a good thing, too, because there are plenty of corpses at Galley House.
Read more
articles.title: The Incident At Galley House review – an enthralling deduction game that can't escape the genre's classic problem

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
It's been just over a year since Oblivion Remastered got update 1.2, a patch aiming to improve its performance and fix a bunch of bugs that'd been floating around since release. Since that point, the Elder Scrolls 4 revamp's been without any major updates, despite problems persisting.
The good news, or potential good news, is that Bethesda have now confirmed that the game's Switch 2 port features "optimisations" they're hoping to bring to PC at some juncture.
Read more
articles.title: Oblivion Remastered's lengthy patch drought could end with its Switch 2 release, which Bethesda say includes "optimisations" they hope to bring to PC

articles.description:
Entertaining open world satire Future? No Thanks! has been abruptly delayed by Steam content reviewers, due to the presence of multiple seconds of "untextured polygons depicting ass and boobs". In a statement, developer Paulo "Molleindustria" Pedercini reveals that Valve's moderation teams have had the game under review for "more than three weeks", but have yet to make a call. Steamworks documentation suggests that content review should take no more than seven business days.

articles.description:
If I've learned anything from years of dark fantasy, it's that there's no force in this universe more terrible than a puny-looking girl with a kitchen knife. Just ask Katana Man, or the Queen of Hearts. Or the lolloping wolfbeast I've recently disembowelled in Rubinite, a pretty slick and engrossingly evil boss rush action game from Gameworks Ventures and Cup Dog Games, which is on sale today.
 Read more

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
If there's anything I know about Steam users, it's that they bloody love that wishlist system. Hundreds, if not thousands of games, all plonked in a single list that we can pretend we'll go through eventually to pick out some corkers we know we'll love, even though we know we'll just play the same thing we always do because the exhaustion of daily life limits what we can take in? Bloody lovely that is! And now, we'll be able to organise that even further, as categories are being added in.
 
Read more
articles.title: Steam wishlists are getting categories, making it even easier to organise all those games you'll definitely buy next sale

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Last week, in the wake of yet another round of mass layoffs across the company, Xbox announced that Fallout 5 is in preproduction, Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters are coming, and that Obsidian are working on a new Fallout project. If you were to ignore the 1600 staffers laid off and the ongoing call for a boycott due to Microsoft providing AI tech to the Israeli military as it continues to bombard Gaza and kill Palestinians, this would possibly be welcome news. But to make matters worse, OneBGS, the Bethesda Game Studios Union, have claimed that on the same day this was announced, laid off workers at Bethesda Montreal were informed that they would "receive the smallest severance legally possible without bargaining with the union."
 
Read more
articles.title: Laid off Bethesda Montreal staff allegedly told they'd get "smallest severance legally possible" the same day as those Fallout announcements

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Ah, the Electronic Entertainment Expo, better known by many as Summer Game Fes-, wait, sorry, guess I've already moved on! Better known as E3, of course, the first of its kind showcase dedicated entirely to video games that died because it simply couldn't figure out how to live in the modern world (they probably should have asked Geoff). The whole thing ended with much more of a whimper than a bang, but once upon a time it was the place to have your game. And now, the Video Game History Foundation have revealed a new collection all about the event "like you've never seen it before," covering many years worth of a range of materials.
 
Read more
articles.title: The Video Game History Foundation's latest collection is a deep dive into E3 "like you've never seen it before"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Waterparks have always felt like quite a strange concept to me in that the UK is small enough that you can just take a quick train ride and be at a beach within an hour or so, give or take. We do have them here, I've just had no reason to go one, and also the idea of having to be rescued from the inside of a slide due to getting stuck for one reason or another is a (I think rational) fear I've had since discovering them. Therefore, I'll take a pass on actually visiting one, but I won't say no to building my own in Aquapark Tycoon, a waterpark sim game that's out in early access today.
 
Read more
articles.title: Forgo visiting the real thing this summer and build the waterpark of your dreams in Aquapark Tycoon, now out in early access

Read more
articles.title: "The goal is to provide what we can": Elder Scrolls Online Crown Store undergoing changes due to "team bandwidth" in wake of Xbox layoffs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced's an idyllic pirate adventure, especially given it trains its eye firmly on Edward Kenway's quest for booty. Naturally, Kenway hangs out with a bunch of real pirates from history throughout his time on the high seas, including the most famous one, Blackbeard. There's now a mod that'll let you play as the bearded buccaneer in Black Flag Resynced. So, here I am to point out a grisly reason you might not fancy getting too into roleplaying as Mr Edward Teach (or Mr Edward Thatch, depending on which accounts you believe).
Read more
articles.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced modders make Blackbeard playable, but here's a syringe-shaped reason to avoid historically accurate pirate roleplay

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
Frosthaven, and Gloomhaven before it, are complex turn-based tactical boardgames. Filled with cards, plastic figurines, a dense rulebook, and a denser tome filled with scenario descriptions and special conditions, Frosthaven's box comes to a weighty 36Ibs, or, in old money, 5Ibs heavier than the Lego Titanic.
One of the perks of the digital adaptations is that you don't need to lug around the equivalent of a four-year-old child to go play at being an RPG adventurer in a frozen wasteland with your mates, you can just boot it up and all hop into a multiplayer server together. Turns, too, play out faster, as you don't need to calculate all the enemy actions and slide their little plastic figurines to their new spots on the board. The digital adaptations reduce this down to a few neatly animated seconds of action. Though, that doesn't mean the rules themselves are any less simple. Nic (RPS in peace) spent a good chunk of his glowing Gloomhaven review just breaking down everything you need to do in a turn. So, understandably, Frosthaven can be difficult for new players to pick up.
However, it's actually the boardgame players trying out Snapshot Games' digital adaptation that are causing more of an issue.
Read more
articles.title: Dear Frosthaven boardgame players complaining the PC tactics RPG adaptation is bugged: the devs say it's likely you've "played it wrong"

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
While it’s not a series of truly Hitman-scale murder sandboxes, 007 First Light does make good on its promise of enabling multiple Bond, James Bonding disciplines: shooting, sneaking, punching, and my personal favourite, getting immediately discovered then bullshitting something about being a door technician for supervillain lairs. But, were it not for some rejigging work on IO Interactive’s part, First Light might well have ended up with an undue preference for the brawling, bloody, Daniel-Craig-in-a-bathroom approach.
That’s according to senior combat designer Tom Marcham, whom I briefly interrogated at a taping of the UKIE’s For One Night Only showcase. Marcham says that although there “was always the idea that [First Light] was going to be this kind of flexible blend” of secret agent styles, in the crucible of active development, the strength of straight up henchman-punching repeatedly threatened to wallop the stealth and social aspects into irrelevance.
Read more
articles.title: "It started to feel like there wasn't any stealth": 007 First Light had to pull Bond's punches to protect IO Interactive's specialty sneaking

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Duh, duh, duh. Duh, duh, de-duh. Duh, duh, duh. Duh, duh. That's how the riff to Deep Purple's tune about a fire burning down a Swiss casino goes. As with any riff, it's just a sequence of inputs you make on your instrument of choice. Usually, this would be a guitar. I've been trying to use the cat piano and singing gnome of jobbing composer sim Offbeat, which is out in early access today, July 22nd. Sadly, I don't think I've cracked it, but I have been having plenty of fun making funky jingles and wedding tunes.
Read more
articles.title: Playing the riff from Smoke on the Water on a cat piano may be possible in composer sim Offbeat, if you've got more musical talent than me

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Hasbro, parent company of Baldur's Gate IP holders Wizards of the Coast and backer of Exodus developers Archetype Entertainment, have announced a $56 million impairment as part of their latest financial results. This recording of assets decreasing in value compared to their theoretical worth is tied to the company having cancelled "several games scheduled for release in 2028 and beyond". That leaves Hasbro's games lineup thinner going forwards, but with releases targeting 2027, like Exodus and Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons, still on the way.
Read more
articles.title: Baldur's Gate series overlords Hasbro take $56 million hit after cancelling several games due out in "2028 and beyond", with Exodus and Warlock unaffected

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Occasionally I will see a game that opts for an artstyle so complex and involved that will clearly take years to make, leaving me with an unbridled fear of the gamey part being not very good. I'm talking about games like Harold Halibut, where the entire thing is stop-motion. Do you know how long stop-motion takes! A while, I've heard. I feel similarly about Scarlet Deer Inn, a Slavic-folklore inspired platformer where every single sprite is made from embroidery that's out today.
 
Read more
articles.title: Scarlet Deer Inn, out now, is a Slavic folk tale platformer with a dark underbelly where every sprite is physically embroidered

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The idea of developing sound and well placed infrastructure in a contemporary city fills me with an overwhelming sense of incompetency, so for the most part I tend to steer clear of city builders of that ilk. I don't want to care about where a hospital needs to go, or how many roads is too many! So something like Thveit, a Norse folklore inspired city builder where the changing seasons shape how your villagers work, seems a bit more my speed.
 
Read more
articles.title: Thveit is a Norse citybuilder filled with folklore creatures where the changing seasons shape how you develop your village

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Things are sounding bad over at Splitgate developer 1047 Games once again. After launching Empulse last month, a wall-running, quite Titanfall-esque FPS with mechs game that James had some fun with, it appears that layoffs have taken place at the studio, marking the third round of them in the space of about a year.
 
Read more
articles.title: Less than a month after launching Empulse, it looks like Splitgate dev 1047 Games are laying off more staff

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I'm sure there's plenty enough of you that moved on from the first Darkest Dungeon onto the second one when that launched in 2023, but guess what! You'll have an opportunity to revisit the original turn-based dungeon crawler next month, as developer Red Hook Studios have announced its first bit of DLC since 2020 in commemoration of the game's 1.0 launch 10th anniversary.
 
Read more
articles.title: Darkest Dungeon is getting its first new bit of DLC in six years, borrowing a couple of classes from its sequel

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Anyone who knows me knows that the one frustration I come back to in games, above all else, more than yellow paint, quest markers and horrendously written dialogue, is that there just isn't enough cow breeding. Where is it? The video game industry is sorely lacking in that department, but fear not fellow freaks, Manor Lords has our back, as by the end of the month you'll be able to breed your cattle to your hearts' content.
 
Read more
articles.title: Manor Lords' next beta update adds what all video games are sorely missing: cow breeding

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Look at the nice fellow in the featured image of this article. Look into his eyes. Look at the slightly awkward grin plastered across his face at the moment in a YouTube video on his channel that I've chosen to pause and take a screenshot. This is a man who wants you to feel "a sense of agony". To be frustrated and perplexed as to which outcome to choose. This is a man who knows you can't feed the world with a set of laser eyeballs. This is Fallout: New Vegas director Josh Sawyer, who recently made some points about RPG building that are worth dissecting in light of his reported new gig as head of Obsidian's upcoming Fallout game.
Read more
articles.title: Reported lead of Obsidian's new Fallout game wants you to feel a "sense of agony" when playing an RPG, rather than being an all-powerful god-splatterer

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
A day will dawn when the premise "what if Darkest Dungeon but also XYZ" will lose its crablike stranglehold on my fancy, but that day is not this day, for today we Dive or Die. Not that the two activities are mutually exclusive. 
In this 2D roguelite scuba sim from Drop Rate Studio and publishers Dear Villagers, the world has succumbed to a "black rain" that inflicts mutations and nightmares. It's been chucking it down for five solid years, in fact, with human civilisation reduced to scraping a living on mountaintops that are now islands. There isn't much of a living to scrape on mountaintops, so off you go into the "abyssal pool" to dredge up some canned food and building materials.
 Read more
articles.title: Out today, Dive or Die is a promising roguelite scuba sim that basically turns Darkest Dungeon into Ecco the Dolphin

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
"Wreckreation wasn’t actually an attempt to recreate Burnout," former Criterion Games studio head Fiona Sperry says as she and her team reveal their latest arcade racer, Wreckreation 2. "I think some people thought it was. But it was actually an exploration of freedom and creativity in racing games, and that was really a continuation of unfinished work at the end of [Burnout] Paradise and also the game we were making before we left EA. It was really about asking the question, ‘What if we gave players an enormous amount of freedom?’"
Read more
articles.title: Building on Burnout and an underwhelming predecessor are Wreckreation 2’s missions, and so far it’s a promising patch of Paradise

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Future? No Thanks! is a jolly and acerbic open world city game from seasoned satirist Paulo "Molleindustria" Perdicini. It's about a bitter old boomer trying to enjoy his final day in an ecosocialist paradise. There's a demo on Steam that gives you 30 minutes access to a realm of sentient toilets, cricket burgers, ornamental park guillotines, and cannabis vending machines. Speaking as a bitter old millennial, I found my 30 minutes delightful.

 
Read more
articles.title: "Enjoy your last day in a future that works for everyone but you": I adore the demo for Future? No Thanks, an open world comedy about a boomer trapped in leftwing paradise

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Forza Horizon 5 creative director Mike Brown, who's currently working on open-world racer Clutch after departing Microsoft-owned Playground Games in 2023, has offered his perspective on Xbox's current layoff-heavy pivot in direction. Despite the Xbox Game Pass push of former Xbox boss Phil Spencer and co being blamed by new boss Asha Sharma as she's ditched studios and given devs their walking papers, Brown still believes Game Pass was a "good" concept, if clearly not one successful enough to avoid this outcome.
Read more
articles.title: "The concept of [Xbox] Game Pass was good" despite its eventual faceplant now contributing to mass job losses, reckons Forza Horizon 5 director

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, this year's Activision shooter about military markspeople (who occasionally look like Beavis and Butt-Head) sliding around with SMGs and shouting 10-4 after checking their corners, is set for pre-release beta testing in August. There are two playtests currently on the calendar, though the first's exclusive to those who pre-order the game.
Read more
articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's open beta is set for next month, and will offer a chance to take on the fearsome new slaying slab mode

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Unity have announced Unity 7, the latest incarnation of their game creation platform. In a pleasant shock for people who've been keeping up with Unity's doings these past couple of years, it doesn't appear to ruin anything. Aside from more routine promises of "speedier workflows" and tastier graffix, the company are promising a more "open" approach whereby collaborators using third-party tools can contribute more easily to Unity projects, without using the full Unity editor. This being the year 2026, there are of course some new features for genAI fans, though Unity appear interestingly guarded on this front, stressing that these can be ignored.
 Read more
articles.title: "Built for that world doesn't mean built to require it": Unity reveal their next game engine while walking a careful line around generative AI

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Former Gears of War and Unreal Tournament designer Cliff Bleszinski has opened up about his struggle with alcoholism and how it's impacted his life and career in game development to this point, as he eyes a possible return to making games. Bleszinski's currently four months sober after suffering a drinking-related seizure in March this year.
Read more
articles.title: "LawBreakers tripped so Concord could faceplant": Gears of War designer Cliff Bleszinski looks back on his career so far and struggle with alcoholism

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
A Florida-based student has been arrested by the FBI after allegedly stealing over $220,000 in cryptocurrency by means of malware-packed free games on Steam.
 Read more
articles.title: FBI accuse Steam user of stealing over $220,000 via malware-infected games like BlockBlasters, Lunara and Dashverse

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Launching a new SSD in the current hardware climate, even a simple, DRAMless, QLC-packing SSD like the Samsung 990, may seem like starting up a roof thatching business during the eruption of Mount Vesuvius: innocuous idea, apocalyptically bad timing.
Read more
articles.title: Samsung 990 review: a lower-spec SSD that’s weirdly great for games

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Sketchy Fables is a first-person explorathon in which, if you kill things with homing butterflies, the world will grow more beautiful, whereas if you kill things with shotguns, the world will slowly succumb to "dark layers filled with loss, decay, and the end of lives". Sure beats Paragon/Renegade.
In a pinch, you can also batter creatures with the stickerbook housing all the bizarre artefacts you've discovered. I'm not sure how weaponising the very inventory contributes to the landscape's transformations, but I do know that I'd like to see this kind of diegetic design in, say, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2, which has menus made of solid wood.
 
Read more
articles.title: First-person explorer Sketchy Fables is a twitchy, teeming feast of hand-drawn art with acting from Hades 2's Sarah Grayson

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
As Oisin reported over the weekend, Steam Machine engineers Yazan Aldehayyat and Pierre-Loup Griffais gave a big Valve thumbs-down to the practice of platform exclusives – a hot topic in the context of Xbox owners Microsoft retreating back into whatever kind of shrivelled, joyless husk Xbox is nowadays. The same interview, with Bloomberg scoopsmith Jason Schreier, also touched on the acutely PC-spoiling subject of RAMnarök and its subsequent, en-masse embiggening of hardware prices. Good news? No! Obviously it’s all terrible!
Read more
articles.title: Valve see the great RAM shortage "getting worse," just in case you were clinging to hopes of a cheaper Steam Machine

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
With Bethesda having begun to dip their fingers into the remaster bucket in recent years, some modders who'd decided long before that to get the ball rolling on such things themselves have had to reckon with the idea that official siblings of their passion projects could be in the works. It happened last year with Skyblivion and Oblivion Remastered, now it's happened for the crew behind The Capital Wasteland Project, an effort to recreate Fallout 3 in Fallout 4, and Fallout 4: New Vegas.
Thankfully, both teams of modders have made clear they plan to keep on trucking with their efforts following the confirmation of the official remasters.
Read more
articles.title: Bethesda's Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters won't stop the modders who've already spent years recreating the RPGs in Fallout 4

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Hello all! This week, there are a lot of new cat-themed games for some reason. One suspects that some dire cat anniversary is underway. Maybe week of 20th July 2026 marks 30 million years since the invention of cats? Or since cats invented us? In any case, there is already far too much cat discourse round these parts, so I've only allowed one of those sinister feline diversions into the Maw. Without further ado, the list.
 Read more
articles.title: This week in PC games: a Mass Effect-style RTS, a gamebook RPG for back-stabbing nobles, and a civilisation builder that offers to teach you kanji

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Game Of Thrones: War For Westeros, the Age of Empiresy RTS teeming with Targaryens and laced with Lannisters, has been delayed to 2027. Developers PlaySide have decided that while development's "progressing well", they need a bit more time to nail their strategical rendition of the Seven Kingdoms.
Read more
articles.title: Game Of Thrones: War For Westeros delayed to 2027, as PlaySide take more time before playing their turn to ensure the RTS hits a "high level of quality"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Sundays are for realising that there's a car in Japan's Super GT racing series this year which is sponsored by horse girl game Umamusume Pretty Derby. Here it is. It's been racing in the GT300 category against, among other cars, a Mercedes sponsored by Hatsune Miku. I'm not sure I like them as much as my all-time favourite GT300 car, the Mooncraft Shiden (I mostly just dig its name), but hey, they exist. I often wonder if their small crews of drivers - Super GT has pilots swap over after a set time behind the wheel - gather at the back of the garages and think about some bloke in the UK writing for a games website. They probably don't.
Read more
articles.title: The Sunday Papers

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
It sounds like IO Interactive's take on the world of James Bond in 007 First Light was going to be quite different at first. Where the game as it currently is focuses on just Mr. Bond, once upon a time there was an idea for it to be something of an ensemble cast, where he would have been working with a number of double-O agents across his missions. Spoilers ahead!
 
Read more
articles.title: "During the training sequence, we make a false promise": IO Interactive on the ensemble James Bond game that 007 First Light never was

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is, if done well, a game that might not land with everybody. For one, there's the lack of a traditional main story quest, and then there's the fact that you only have 30 in-game days and nights to beat it. Neither are necessarily massively novel, the brilliant Unsighted, for example, also forces a timer upon you, but this is still a notable AAA game taking a risk. This thing likely won't have been cheap to make, and crafting a scenario where not everyone is going to experience the entirety of what it offers, on purpose, is certainly a touch bold at the very least. So it's a good thing its director is happy with people missing things.
 
Read more
articles.title: You're probably not going to see everything your friend does in The Blood of Dawnwalker, and its director is just fine with that

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The Steam Machine is going to sit in an odd place when it arrives. It's technically a PC, but shaped and presented like a console, which is obviously the whole point. But it differs from most traditional consoles in that it won't be coming with any games exclusive to the hardware. That's because for Valve, they want the Steam Machine to be as open as possible.
 
Read more
articles.title: Valve aren't putting any exclusives on the Steam Machine because they see "the whole PC catalog as our 'launch exclusive'"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Another regular day in Marathon Land. Following on from mass layoffs at Bungie after the final major update for Destiny 2, and ahead of next week's mid-season 2 Marathon patch, the extraction shooter's game director Joe Ziegler has announced that he's left the studio, with Del Chafe III taking over his role. Chafe, up until this point, has served as Marathon's assistant game director.
 
Read more
articles.title: A month after mass layoffs at Bungie, Marathon game director Joe Ziegler is leaving the studio

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
It's been almost two months since ZA/UM released their second game Zero Parades: For Dead Spies (and obviously first after years of controversy. Unfortunately for workers at the studio, the game does not appear to have sold well enough, as more than 30 devs are being laid off or are at-risk of being laid off.
 
Read more
articles.title: ZA/UM are set for more layoffs only two months after launching Zero Parades: For Dead Spies

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Which way are you voting in the election?
There’s an election coming, could I trouble you to ask which way you’re voting?
ELECTION. YOU. VOTING? WHICH WAY?
The time to place the great slip of paper into the holy box of ballots is almost nigh, my honoured friend, wherefore will thou be placing thine vote and whom will it be in favour of?
There are a lot of ways you can ask someone which way they plan to vote. All of them are awkward. The awkwardness isn’t helped by the fact that, in these situations, you might be standing on a doorstep having just interrupted their dinner or be butting into a chat they were having in the street with someone they actually like. Esoteric Ebb revels in that awkwardness.
Read more
articles.title: Esoteric Ebb is the D&Disco Elysium I never knew I needed, but more importantly it's proof I'll never be cut out for political canvassing

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
What are we all playing this weekend?
This weekend is the eye of the wedding storm, a brief reprieve before heading up to Sheffield next week for further nuptials. Though, that doesn't mean I can relax. My body is in a finely tuned state that I can't let slacken with the finish line is in sight.
I will, of course, be following my wedding guest training regime.
Read more
articles.title: What are we all playing this weekend?

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Following Microsoft's mass layoffs, Bethesda have clearly been told to be a bit more active in communicating exactly what they've got in the works. Cue a big blog post announcing that Fallout 5's in preproduction alongside the studio's main focus, The Elder Scrolls 6, with both being assembled on a version of the Creation engine put together following Starfield's launch. Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas remasters have also been confirmed to be on the way, though with no concrete release dates as of yet.
Read more
articles.title: Fallout 5 is in preproduction alongside The Elder Scrolls 6's development, while Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas remasters are on the way, Bethesda confirm

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
The original Suzerain, a political strategy game presented as a visual novel, cast you in the role of Anton Rayne, the newly elected President of fictional country Sordland. You had to tackle political turmoil as the leader of a country coming out of years of authoritarian rule, while also dealing with an economic crisis, and threats from the powerful nations neighbouring your borders. In the Kingdom of Rizia DLC, you left elected politics behind and, instead, sat in the inherited throne as King Romus Toras. Though your absolute power was tempered by anti-monarchists, breakaway states, and corrupt vassals.
The stakes in new DLC Suzerain Stories: The Neutral Lens are significantly smaller. You are just a journalist, Ilias Moris, the anchor on international news program The Neutral Lens. The decisions you make don't restrict trade in ports, pass laws that limit freedoms, or send citizens to war. Instead you're picking what question to ask in an interview or where to send your reporters for a scoop.
But how much impact decisions the press can make on the world is exactly the point.
Read more
articles.title: "I'm saying this on camera and millions of people will believe it": How Suzerain Stories: The Neutral Lens lets you shape the news

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
Answering concerns that The Sims team may face pressure to reduce support for diversity following the Saudi Arabian-backed buyout of EA, senior character artist Jess Hyland says she's not "heard anything" about such a mandate and, if one were introduced, she "would fight it tooth and nail."
Read more
articles.title: "I would fight it tooth and nail": The Sims artist would challenge any mandate to reduce diversity after EA Saudi buyout

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The Communications Workers of America (CWA) union and their Canadian offshoot CWA Canada have filed unfair labour practice complaints against Microsoft, accusing the company of having mishandled the recent mass layoffs at Xbox.
Read more
articles.title: Unions accuse Microsoft of having "unlawfully fired people" in unfair labor practice complaints filed over Xbox layoffs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
While reports about Microsoft's mass layoffs have painted a devastating picture, the company and affected studios like Doom developers Id Software have been publicly trying to reassure players that the cuts aren't the end of the world. Doom: The Dark Ages director Hugo Martin has stuck to that line while acknowledging the layoffs during on official livestream of the game's Revelations DLC, which came out the same week 136 Id workers were shown the door.
Read more
articles.title: "Id Tech is there, the Doom team is here": Doom: The Dark Ages director pushes back against idea studio have been "nerfed into the ground" by Xbox layoffs

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The idea of another person controlling every action my body takes is one that keeps me awake at night more often than I like to acknowledge to myself. So how about a game all about that! It's called Remote Control, and in it you most titularly remote control human proxies to explore a derelict spaceship and figure out what went wrong on it.
 
Read more
articles.title: Control a human proxy on an abandoned spaceship by typing in every command or risk losing your job in Remote Control

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I've never been a football person, so this whole Global Mug thing that's going on at the moment is as important to me as eyelids for a fish. What I have always been is someone who likes platformers, however, even when they're all about that thing they call the beautiful game. And in the case of Kick, it seems that sidescrolling ball dribbling is actually quite delightful.
 
Read more
articles.title: I don't like football, but I do like platformers, so Kick is a pretty little bridge that closes that gap

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Marathon's already announced mid-season 2 update is set to arrive next week, bringing with it the shooter's first proper, albeit experimental, PvE mode, Vault Breaker. A new blog post has gone into a bit more detail as to what you can expect with the new update, with a teaser trailer showing off some extra bits, but the biggest bummer is the fact that Vault Breaker will only be around for a short while.
 
Read more
articles.title: Marathon's experimental PvE roguelite mode is, bafflingly, only around for two weeks when it drops next week

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Outside of the entirety of the ocean, the thing that probably scares me most about the things the world produces are natural disasters. You're telling me that sometimes the wind gets so fast it can pick up a dang cow? I'm smaller than a cow! I'd have no chance. And it's this fear that I, and I assume many of you, have that sits at the core of Funnel Runners, an online co-op game where you have to fix up a fan to escape a massive tornado.
 
Read more
articles.title: Fix up your van with a bunch of your best pals and escape an onslaught of tornados in survival co-op game Funnel Runners

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
As strange as it might sound, there truly might be no better piece of writing to turn into an anime girl roguelike than Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy. It's the original self-insert fic after all (arguably, anyway), so why shouldn't Hell Maiden put its own little spin on it? That's the nature of these sorts of works. And today, you'll be able to get a bigger taste of the game and see if it's able to pull all of this off, as it's now out in early access.
 
Read more
articles.title: Roguelike bullet heaven Divine Comedy but with anime girls Hell Maiden is out today in early access

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
"Play is humanity's oldest technology for connection and learning," Roblox's CEO yells at me through my monitor. "Before agriculture, before commerce, before civilization, we played together." Right, so, where's this going? Oh. They're rolling out a tool on their mobile app which allows people to generate basic games by sticking a text prompt into an AI model, then do some light rearranging of said game so they can pretend it's in any way unique or artful before they publish it for others to give a go. The tool's called Build.
Read more
articles.title: Roblox announce plans to let people AI generate basic games using text prompts stuck into a mobile app, but claim that won't fill their homepage with AI slop

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
GOG, famed revampers of classic PC games, have done just that to the Gold edition of beloved purse-snatching stealth romp Thief: The Dark Project. Through the storefront's preservation program, the GOG version of Thief Gold boasts a number of handy tweaks to help it run seamlessly on modern hardware.
Read more
articles.title: Thief Gold with updated graphics and integrated modern controller support is the latest addition to GOG's preservation program, ahead of Nightdive's full remaster

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Last week's Microsoft layoffs, a seemingly never-ending source of terrible and sobering news, included several members of the Elder Scrolls Online's leadership team. According to a WARN notice, studio head Jo Burba is among those departing, despite having only stepped into that role around the time of last year's mass layoffs at Microsoft. With him and several other key figures on the outs, a "transition" to a new leadership team for the MMO is reportedly underway.
Read more
articles.title: Xbox's gut-wrenching layoffs include the Elder Scrolls Online dev who became studio head around the time of last year's gut-wrenching Xbox layoffs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
We've all been there. You're a pirate captain whose pockets are overflowing with freshly nicked doubloons and you fancy blowing it all on some shiny new cannons or a figurehead carved to resemble a bag of money. So, you sail on down to a port with a harbourmaster and start perusing ship upgrades. Then, when you get back to the docks, your ship's disappeared into thin air. Ah. Yarr've got to be kidding me. Completing the rest of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced might be rather difficult now. Thankfully, these impromptu mutinies are a bug Ubisoft have fixed in the title update set to arrive in the game today.
Read more
articles.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced's latest update stops unexpected mutinies triggered by ship shopping trips and forces skies to be sunnier

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
Last week, to mark its 30th anniversary, EA rebranded Criterion as Criterion: A Battlefield Studio. The storied studio that created Burnout and in recent years has shepherded the Need For Speed series, as well as working on the rebooted Star Wars: Battlefront, will become just one of the four studios supporting EA's fresh Battlefield push.
This isn't the first time Criterion have contributed to Battlefield, the Guildford studio have been involved since 2015's Battlefield 1, but the rebranding marks an end to working on other projects.
Or is it?
Read more
articles.title: "Never say never": Criterion aren't ruling out a return to Need For Speed, but Battlefield is their only focus for now

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
I fear I’ve authored some kind of Boy Who Cried Wolf situation, vis à vis Denshattack. It’s shown signs of greatness ever since its reveal last year, but in hindsight, I wonder if my enthusiasm for its silly side – it is undeniably a game about trains doing skateboard-style flips and grinds, sometimes while chased by giant baseballs – ever contributed to an impression of it as a mere novelty. A joke game, disinterested in anything beyond breakneck wackiness.
I hope not. Because Denshattack is utterly and genuinely brilliant, and not just because it lets you blow up an AI data centre by ploughing a locomotive through it.
Read more
articles.title: Denshattack review: one of 2026's best games so far is a racing ruckus of railways, rebellion, and ramen

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The wait for GTA 6 on PC lasting past this November's been a foregone conclusion for a while now, but if you're interested in a bit of developer perspective as to why Rockstar opt to do things that way, a former producer at the company's offered some. Essentially, it's a matter of it being less of a headache to scale up after initially getting a game working on hardware with stricter limitations than it would be to strip back an all-singing, all-dancing PC port for consoles.
Read more
articles.title: As GTA 6's PC portless launch looms, ex-Rockstar producer says prioritising consoles first is primarily about being "better off starting with the constraints"

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
"For the longest time, we went one by one," Ata Sergey Nowak, co-founder of Torpor Games, the studio behind strategy game Suzerain, tells me, explaining the four year gap between the game's release and its first DLC. "Our games take a long time, our staff was very limited, and our financing was very project-to-project." So it was a little surprising he was also telling me Torpor are today announcing not one but three new projects - two DLCs and a spin-off. All of which are due to be released before their next flagship title, The Conformist.
Each of the three newly announced projects will take you deeper into the world of Suzerain, and let you see its states and people from new perspectives. But, Torpor aren't only making these games to expand Suzerain, they're also using it as a defence against a punishing industry.
Read more
articles.title: "We've seen how close you can get": How studio closures pushed Suzerain's maker to create two new DLCs and a turn-based strategy spinoff

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Dead Space creator Glen Schofield has decided it's time to walk away from game development, or at least "the day-to-day work of making them. Thus concludes a career which kicked off all the way back in the early 90s, and saw Schofield work on games ranging from Disney World racing to Call of Duty and The Callisto Protocol. The latter will now go down as the developer's last game, provided he hasn't got any surprise un-retirements up his sleeves.
Read more
articles.title: Dead Space creator Glen Schofield announces he's retiring from "the day-to-day work" of making games while in the vicinity of some chirpy nature

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
A fresh report has shed light on what played out behind the scenes last week as Microsoft laid off around 1600 people and parted ways with a number of studios. While news of the various affects the cuts have had on specific studios still under the Xbox banner since that pint, the report also paints a damning picture of the effect these layoffs and the ones which still loom have had on the mindset of remaining workers, with unclear goals having contributed to a situation whereby staff feel they're disposable regardless of what they make.
Read more
articles.title: "There are no benefits to being owned by Microsoft": Xbox owners accused of cultivating a "disposable worker mentality" in damning report on layoffs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Today, July 15th, unionised Microsoft workers are set to hold a series of co-ordinated rallies outside the offices of Xbox-owned studios, in protest of the mass layoffs the company set in motion last week. According to the Communications Workers of America union (CWA), over 400 union-represented jobs across Bethesda Game Studios, ZeniMax, and id Software are being cut. In solidarity with the union marches, modders continue to fill Bethesda games with union logos. Skyrim was the first and Fallout 4's the latest.
Read more
articles.title: As unionised Microsoft workers rally against Bethesda layoffs, Fallout 4's been filled with protest signs and OneBGS logoed vault suits by modders

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
There is an anxiety to deckbuilders that I don't find with many other games, in that I get incredibly stressed about which cards I should play. I feel this way about card games in real life too, for reasons I truly cannot understand. It's just a game! And yet I can't help but scold my tiny, silly brain in moments where I pull the wrong move. So I am quite keen on how Grail sounds, the latest little game from little game aficionados Sokpop, where after you build your deck, the deck does the fighting for you.
 
Read more
articles.title: Deckbuilder Grail quells the fear in my heart of playing the wrong card by pinning all of the strategy on the deckbuilding

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
RuneScape is having a bit of a home improvement moment, quite literally. An update went live yesterday that focused completely on player-owned housing, revamping how you both use and construct it, bringing it honestly quite close to The Sims in how it handles house building, amongst other tweaks and additions.
 
Read more
articles.title: RuneScape revamps its housing customisation with a snazzy looking build mode and the option to make your own neighbourhood with your pals

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Dragon's Dogma 2's fast travel system is a pain in the ass, and depending on who you ask and even when you ask it, this is a good, bad, fine, annoying, interesting, frustrating, clever thing. But as part of a recent free update that has arrived in the leadup to the game's Dark Arisen expansion, it is now less of a pain in the ass. And for the expansion's producer Naoto Oyama and director Kenta Kinoshita, it's about giving people more choices.
 
Read more
articles.title: With Dragon's Dogma 2's new infinite fast travel, Dark Arisen's director wants you to know they're "not forcing" you to use it

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Another step forward has been made by IWGB Game Workers in their efforts towards calling for Grand Theft Auto 6 developer Rockstar Games to formally recognise the studio's union. A new letter addressed to Rockstar studio director Jennifer Kolbe and head of HR Rob Spampinato has been signed by 22 trade union leaders joining in the call for the developer to start bargaining with the IWGB.
 
Read more
articles.title: 22 trade union leaders have signed a letter joining the call for GTA 6 developer Rockstar to recognise the IWGB Game Workers union

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Those of you that have been playing Slay the Spire 2 in its current early access form will have seen that some of the placeholder art looks, well, arguably bad. I am not necessarily making this argument! But it could be made. As it turns out, according to Mega Crit co-founder Casey Yano, this is very much the point, and has more purpose behind it than just being easier to do.
 
Read more
articles.title: "They would feel a kind of sadness, right?": Slay the Spire 2 dev on using slightly rubbish placeholder art over AI

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Following the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced, an undertaking by a bunch of Ubisoft studios based all over the world, union protests at one of said studios have kicked off over plans to lay off staff now the remake's out of the door. Ubisoft Barcelona, the studio in question, were reported last month to be set for a restructure that'd see them focus solely on Rainbow Six games going forwards.
Read more
articles.title: "Ubisoft thinks that's what we deserve": Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced's release followed by union strike over planned Ubisoft Barcelona layoffs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
While there's never been any shortage of characters who'll pay you to splatter some brains across the desert with your trusty anti-mat rifle in Fallout: New Vegas, a new mod adds a whole extra faction based around being a post-apocalyptic assassin. They're dubbed the Dark Family, and you get no prizes for guessing which robed gang of Elder Scrolls dagger-enthusiasts they're based on.
Read more
articles.title: Fallout: New Vegas gets a Mojave interpretation of Oblivion's Dark Brotherhood, thanks to this assassin-focused faction quest mod

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
2026 has already had a modern take on James Bond in game form thanks to IO Interactive's 007 First Light, and now it's getting some retro bondage thanks to a throwback spy FPS that's been in the works for a while. Agent 64: Spies Never Die, a GoldenEye-inspired romp from solo developer Replicant D6, releases next month.
Read more
articles.title: GoldenEye-inspired FPS Agent 64: Spies Never Die finally releases in August, complete with optional big heads

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Having recently parted ways with former owners Xbox as part of the console maker's mass cuts, South of Midnight and We Happy Few developers Compulsion Games have announced they're seeking opportunities to collaborate with other studios. Likely to help them keep the lights on until they've got a new game of their own well on its way, Compulsion look to have turned their focus towards landing a co-development or support gig on someone else's project.
Read more
articles.title: Following Xbox split, South of Midnight devs Compulsion are looking for work as a co-development or support studio

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The IWGB union have held a protest with former Build a Rocket Boy (BARB) staff outside of the MindsEye studio's offices. The union accused the company of hosting an expenses-paid fan playtest event following layoffs, with IWGB chair Spring McParlin-Jones dubbing it "a kick in the teeth for the fired workers who are seeing fans brought in to do jobs that would otherwise have been theirs".
Read more
articles.title: "A kick in the teeth for the fired workers": Unionised former MindsEye devs protest alleged fan playtest at Build A Rocket Boy

articles.author: Sin Vega
articles.description:
LESBIANS
BAGPIPES
STREAMING
LET'S GO!
Read more
articles.title: Rally Point: I am extremely here for turn-based strategy game The Great Villainess, and not just for gay reasons

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Good news! Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls' Steam backend no longer lists it as not being available for purchase in 132 countries. It's now only listed it as not being available for purchase in 117 countries. That's 15 whole countries removed from the list of excluded nations, which looks like it could be linked in some way to the need to have PSN account to access certain bits of the game.
Read more
articles.title: Well, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is now only barred from purchase in 117 countries according to Steam's backend, which is a start

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Last week, Avowed and The Outer Worlds 2 developers Obsidian lost around quarter of their staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs. The studio were subsequently reported to be pivoting to start work on a new Fallout game helmed by New Vegas director Josh Sawyer, with a sequel to Avowed all but canned in the process. Cue, naturally, people like me discussing what sort of game the shift towards a new Fallout all these years after New Vegas could result in, and also some voices declaring that Obsidian just aren't as good as they used to be.
Outer Worlds 2 director Brandon Adler, naturally, disagrees with the latter group of loudmouths.
Read more
articles.title: Obsidian still have "the same DNA" that went into New Vegas and KOTOR 2, The Outer Worlds 2 director insists, following chatter around layoffs

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: ČD - Telematika)
articles.description: V dnešním díle Postřehů se podíváme na koncové šifrování, které Discord zapíná a Instagram naopak vypíná, na únik přístupových klíčů americké agentury CISA na GitHubu a na dvě mezinárodní policejní operace.
articles.title: Postřehy z bezpečnosti: AI jako pomocník, záškodník i dobrodruh

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Filip Zatloukal)
articles.description: FreeBSD odstranilo ze svého základního kódu poslední zbytky kódu pod licencí GNU GPL. Operační systém Haiku portuje monitor virtuálních strojů z NetBSD. Nadace UBports vydala dlouho očekávanou aktualizaci Ubuntu Touch OTA-2.0.
articles.title: FreeBSD odstranilo kód pod GNU GPL, Haiku portuje NVMM

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Týden v KDE a nejen automatické zamknutí RDP sezení při ztrátě připojení, týden v GNOME a opět Sophie s Loupe + Glycin či applovské menu Kiwi, vývojová verze Wine 11.14 a konverze 7.1 zvuku.
articles.title: Vylepšení pro knihovnu Glycin a cenzura PDF pro GNOME, Wine řeší nejen běh Hedgewars

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Úpravy kódu systémových volání jednodušší život vývojářům Linuxu, další základní desky Asus s podporu čtení dat ze senzorů, cílené vypínání přehřátých CPU jader pro Intel, sekundární grafická pipe pro moderní APU od AMD.
articles.title: Linuxové jádro 7.3 přinese vypínání CPU jader Intel a zefektivnění běhu AMD APU

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Pavel Tišnovský)
articles.description: Na sběrnici SIO se připojovala i externí paměťová média. Většina z nich představuje dosti fascinující propojení analogové a digitální techniky. Dnes se zaměříme na magnetická média, především na kazetové magnetofony.
articles.title: Sběrnice SIO pro počítače Atari a problematika externích paměťových médií

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jiří Eischmann)
articles.description: AI tento rok naplno vtrhla do vývoje softwaru a výrazně ovlivňuje také open-source projekty. V open source v poslední době v souvislosti s AI pozoruji některé trendy, které svět otevřeného softwaru mění.
articles.title: AI mění svět open source: zahlcení, inflace projektů a klesající motivace

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jiří Sluka)
articles.description: Uklidíme dotfiles do profilů, necháme si vygenerovat čerstvý mirrorlist pro pacman, vytiskneme zdrojáky s náhledem přímo v terminálu, dáme čtyřem AI agentům jednu společnou paměť a nakonec proměníme terminál v hackerskou scénu z filmu.
articles.title: Softwarová sklizeň (22. 7. 2026): vytiskněte zdrojové kódy se zvýrazněním syntaxe

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Pavel Tišnovský)
articles.description: Už jsme se věnovali popisu knihovny gg určené pro vykreslování 2D grafiky. Dnes popis dokončíme a navíc se zmíníme o knihovnách gg-pdf a gg-svg sloužící k exportu 2D grafiky do vektorových formátů PDF a SVG.
articles.title: Tvorba 2D i 3D grafiky a animací v Go s využitím projektu GoGPU (2. část)

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: CESNET CERTS)
articles.description: Pozrieme sa na to, ako sa dá jediným e-mailom prepísať pamäť AI agenta, ako sa dá agentovi klamať, čo dokáže cudzie rozšírenie v prehliadači a prečo AI útočník naletí na návnadu ochotnejšie než človek.
articles.title: Postrehy z bezpečnosti: AI agentom sa nedá veriť ani vlastná pamäť

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Filip Zatloukal)
articles.description: Byl představen projekt Holo Core, oficiální portu Arch Linuxu pro ARM64, který bude tvořit základ operačního systému připravovaného VR headsetu Steam Frame. Od září 2026 bude Google na Androidu blokovat software třetích stran.
articles.title: Arch Linux pro Steam Frame, Google uzavírá Android

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jan Fikar)
articles.description: Ubuntu vychází z Debianu a má z historických důvodů stále soubor /etc/debian_version.  Ten obsahuje například forky/sid pro 26.04 nebo trixie/sid pro 24.04. To samozřejmě neodpovídá skutečnosti a může to některé nástroje mást. Správně se má používat  /etc/os-release.
articles.title: Ubuntu se zbaví artefaktu /etc/debian_version

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: johny)
articles.description: Kanál CultRepo minulý týždeň priniesol nový dokumentárny film The Java Story. Dokument podrobne mapuje viac než 30-ročnú históriu jedného z najvplyvnejších programovacích jazykov na svete. Film prináša spomienky a pohľady priamo od tvorcov, inžinierov a kľúčových osobností — vrátane Jamesa Goslinga, architektov Briana Goetza či Marka Reinholda a mnohých ďalších.
articles.title: Nový dokumentárny film The Java Story

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jan Fikar)
articles.description: Kvůli bezpečnostním problémům bude v jádře 7.3 omezeno rozhraní AF_ALG. Některé aplikace jako například iwd, bluez a cryptsetup jej stále používají. Tyto aplikace budou v jádře 7.3 whitelistovány a půjde je používat ve výchozím nastavení. Nicméně by všechny aplikace měly přejít na kryptografické knihovny v uživatelském prostoru.
articles.title: Cryptsetup 2.8.7 bude fungovat i bez AF_ALG

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Jan Fikar)
articles.description: Qualys našel v jádře pomocí nástroje Claude Mythos další zranitelnost. Tentokrát se týká souborového systému XFS s podporou reflink, což je v jádře od verze 4.11 z roku 2017. Chyba je vedena jako CVE-2026–64600. Jde o chybu souběhu, neprivilegovaný lokální útočník může zapsat do souborů na XFS, ke kterým nemá práva. Takovým způsobem může získat například oprávnění roota.
articles.title: Nová lokální zranitelnost jádra RefluXFS, hrozí přepsání souborů a elevace práv

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Redakce)
articles.description: Linuxových systémů přibývá, každý den se spouštějí nové servery a někdo se o ně musí starat. To znamená spoustu různých dovedností specifických právě pro linuxové prostředí. Jak to zprovoznit, kudy bezpečně dovnitř, co tam najdeme, jak se o to postaráme a jak to nastavíme nebo rozšíříme.
articles.title: Naučte se používat Linux správně a bezpečně (školení)

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Od pondělí 27. července 2026 sníží GitHub finanční odměny v rámci programu Bug Bounty u všech úrovní závažnosti nejméně o polovinu. Odměny za kritické chyby klesnou z 20 000 až 30 000 dolarů na pevnou částku 10 000 dolarů. V rámci úrovně VIP, do které se lze dostat pouze na pozvání, budou vypláceny odměny ve výši 30 000 dolarů nebo více.
articles.title: GitHub snižuje odměny za hlášení chyb

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Seth Larson, bezpečnostní vývojář v Python Software Foundation, oznámil, že Python Package Index (PyPI) bude nově odmítat nové soubory nahrané do verzí starších než 14 dní. Toto omezení má zabránit zneužití (doslova otrávení) starých verzí v případě, že dojde k narušení bezpečnosti publikačních tokenů nebo pracovních postupů projektů na PyPI.
articles.title: PyPI nyní odmítá nahrání nových souborů po 14 dnech od vydání

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Vývojáři Mozilly uvolnili novou verzi e-mailového klienta Thunderbird s číslem 153.  Mezi hlavní novinky patří vylepšená podpora sjednocených složek, která umožňuje zobrazovat barevný indikátor účtu s názvem účtu, podpora otevírání přihlašovacího okna OAuth pro e-mailové účty ve výchozím webovém prohlížeči a podpora využívání služeb Thundermail bez nutnosti instalace doplňku.
articles.title: Mozilla Thunderbird 153 integruje službu Thundermail a vylepšuje OAuth

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Společnost Canonical spustila nový Enterprise Store určený pro organizace, které potřebují lepší kontrolu nad distribucí Ubuntu v podnikových sítích, regulovaných prostředích a systémech odpojených od veřejné sítě.
articles.title: Canonical představil Enterprise Store pro správu softwaru v uzavřených sítích

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Vývojáři jádra zveřejnili mezi 19. a 20. červencem 2026 celkem 432 záznamů CVE, které se přidávají k více než čtyřiceti dalším v tomto měsíci. Takové množství vede odborníky na bezpečnost v poštovní konferenci oss-security k otázce, zda je stále možné stanovovat priority jednotlivých oprav jádra podle čísel CVE.
articles.title: Vývojáři linuxového jádra přidělili 432 CVE během dvou dnů

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Open-source projekt Playstation 3 emulátoru RPCS3 přidává podporu běhu na dalších Radeonech, a to až po řadu HD 2000 z éry před téměř 20 lety. Obecně pod tímto emulátorem běží už tři čtvrtiny her, které na Playstation 3 vyšly, do budoucna je v plánu samozřejmě tento počet nadále navyšovat, plus odstranit závislost na firmwaru této konzole. Nově byl také implementován modul cellSysmodule.
articles.title: Emulátor Playstation 3, RPCS3, podporuje ještě starší Radeony, ale za cenu výkonnostních kompromisů

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Canonical zveřejnil informace o třech zranitelnostech postihujících snapd. Dvě označuje s vysokým dopadem, třetí je považována za střední – avšak zase její přítomnost v Ubuntu sahá až do roku 2016 a vydání Ubuntu 16.04 LTS.
articles.title: Tři zranitelnosti v Ubuntu Snap, jedna sahající až k Ubuntu 16.04 LTS

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Projekt desktopového prostředí GNOME zavádí některé změny ve fungování. První se týká zkrácení lhůty pro zveřejnění nahlášených zranitelností, která dosud měla velmi velkorysou lhůtu 90 dní. Nově bude vše zveřejněno po 30 dnech. GNOME chyby tohoto typu opravuje obvykle do jednoho až tří týdnů a 90denní lhůta tak vše zbytečně natahovala (informaci přináší Michael Catanzaro z Red Hatu, který má na starosti bezpečnostní záležitosti v GNOME).
articles.title: GNOME mění přístup nejen k AI hlášením chyb

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Před necelými dvěma lety představilo Raspberry Pi svůj dotykový displej Touch Display 2 ve velikosti 7" a rozlišením 720×1280. Vloni v létě byl představen jeho menší 5" bratříček se stejným rozlišením. Nyní byla do rodiny přidána 10" varianta, jejíž cena byla stanovena na 80 dolarů. V českých obchodech se bude prodávat zhruba za dva tisíce korun.
articles.title: Nový 10″ dotykový displej Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2 za 80 dolarů

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: johny)
articles.description: Zakladateľ Linuxu Linus Torvalds sa v júli 2026 v komunitnej diskusii jasne vyjadril na adresu kritikov umelej inteligencie. Diskusia sa rozvinula v reakcii na návrh zapojiť AI nástroj Sashiko (vyvíjaný v Google) do automatizovaného preverovania vývojárskych opráv.
articles.title: Linus Torvalds odkazuje: Linux nie je anti-AI projekt

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Redakce)
articles.description: Chceš začít s programováním? Python je oblíbený programovací jazyk mezi vývojáři i zaměstnavateli a zároveň super vstupenka do světa programování. Nauč se přemýšlet jako programátor a efektivně využívat Python na řešení nejrůznějších problémů. Online Python Akademie znamená celkem 6 měsíců studia jednou týdně nebo tři měsíce dvakrát týdně. Následující kurz začíná 3. září.
articles.title: Online Python Akademie: začněte s programováním v oblíbeném jazyce (online kurz)

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Uzákonění celorepublikového zákazu mobilních telefonů ve školách navrhl ministr školství Robert Plaga a na svém jednání jej dle očekávaní podpořila celá současná vláda ČR. Na tiskové konferenci o výsledku informoval premiér a školství tak nyní čeká poslední školní rok, kdy mohou žáci své smartphony ve škole používat.
articles.title: Žáci ZŠ od 1. září 2027 bez mobilů ve škole, schválila vláda

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Fedora Engineering and Steering Committee (FESCo) schválila návrh, aby s podzimním vydáním Fedora 45 přišla i podpora instalací využívající Stratis. Podpora bude součástí instalátoru Anaconda pro Fedoru.
articles.title: Fedora 45 přijde na podzim s podporou Stratis v instalátoru

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: David Ježek)
articles.description: Phoronix připomíná sadu patchů, která v poslední době prodělala spousty revizí a která definitivně míří do Direct Rendering Manager (DRM) subsystému linuxového jádra. Jde o zavedení podpory tzv. cold reset recovery pro DRM ovladače, s prvotní implementací pro ovladač Intel Xe.
articles.title: V přípravě Cold Reset Recovery pro GPU Intel

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Svatopluk Vít)
articles.description: Nintendo podle žalobců usiluje o dvojí kompenzaci za stejná cla - jednou od zákazníků a podruhé od americké vlády. Společnost s tím nesouhlasí a nově požádala soud o zamítnutí celé žaloby.
articles.title: Nintendo chce zastavit žalobu hráčů kvůli vraceným clům

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Fero Volar)
articles.description: Na 23. září 2026 je do bratislavské Nové Cvernovky naplánovaná jednodenní konference #nobullshit.camp pro tech leadery, DevOps a platform inženýry. Mají tu zaznít upřímné příběhy z praxe o tom, co v produkčních systémech reálně fungovalo, co se pokazilo a co si z toho lidé odnesli. Témata pokrývají tři oblasti – DevOps a platformy (Kubernetes, cloud, provoz systémů), firemní kulturu a leadership.
articles.title: Konference #nobullshit.camp nabídne příběhy z praxe DevOps a platform inženýrů

articles.author: redakce@root.cz (Root.cz: Petr Krčmář)
articles.description: Vývojáři po necelém půlroce vydali novou verzi nástroje pro konfiguraci síťových rozhraní NetworkManager 1.58. Vylepšení se dočkal nástroj nmtui pro konfiguraci v textovém uživatelském rozhraní, který získal možnost vyhledávání sítí nebo jejich sdílení mezi zařízeními prostřednictvím QR kódu.

articles.author: Ladislav Hagara
articles.description:
Evropská komise (EK) vyměřila americké internetové společnosti Google pokutu 890 milionů eur (21,5 miliardy Kč) za porušení unijního nařízení o digitálních trzích (DMA). Firma se podle unijní exekutivy provinila tím, že ve vyhledávači Google Search upřednostňovala vlastní služby a že podnikům ukládala omezení, která jim bránila nasměrovat spotřebitele k alternativním, často levnějším nákupním kanálům na platformě Google Play. 

Prezident společnosti Google pro globální záležitosti Kent Walker podrobil postup Evropské komise kritice a uvedl, že dnešní rozhodnutí bude mít negativní dopady na evropské spotřebitele i podniky.

„Abychom splnili požadavky, musíme odstranit funkce vyhledávání v reálném čase, které Evropané milují. Například okamžité ceny a dostupnost hotelů, letů a restaurací,“ uvedl Walker. Firma podle něj bude muset rovněž omezit bezpečnostní opatření v obchodě Google Play

„Není to poctivá konkurence. Je to zhoršování produktu vynucené malou skupinou stěžovatelů sledujících vlastní zájmy, což bude mít negativní dopad na evropské podniky a spotřebitele. Regulace by měla produkty zlepšovat, ne zhoršovat,“ prohlásil rovněž Walker.
articles.title: Brusel vyměřil Googlu pokutu 890 milionů eur za zvýhodňování vlastních služeb
